mainTopic: תנור של עכנאי, the power of אונאת דברים, and not hurting a גר
overview: This amud finishes the story of the תנור של עכנאי. רבי אליעזר brings every argument and then miracles to prove his view: a carob tree, a stream, the walls of the בית המדרש, and finally a בת קול. רבי יהושע answers 'לא בשמים היא': the תורה was given at סיני, and it tells us to follow the majority. אליהו later reports that הקדוש ברוך הוא smiled and said, 'My children have defeated Me.' The חכמים then place רבי אליעזר in נידוי, and his pain brings damage to the world. In the end רבן גמליאל dies, because the gates of Heaven are always open to someone hurt by words. The גמרא then teaches that hurting or oppressing a גר breaks three לאוין, and that we must not insult a גר, since we were strangers in מצרים ourselves. Finally, a new משנה begins about not mixing batches of produce when selling.

steps.title: The oven gets its name
steps.stepSummary: The oven that רבי אליעזר and the חכמים argued about is known as the 'oven of עכנאי'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the oven of עכנאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing the earlier quote about the segmented oven by giving it its famous name. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument was about an oven built from separate rings with sand between them. רבי אליעזר said it is טהור, because it is not a real single vessel, and the חכמים said it can become טמא. Here the oven gets a nickname, and the גמרא will explain that nickname next.

phrases.english: And this is the oven of akhnai.
phrases.notes: This is the oven made of rings with sand between them, from the case just quoted before this.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the quoted משנה about the segmented oven.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The disputed segmented oven is called 'the oven of עכנאי'.

steps.title: Why call it a snake?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the name עכנאי means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'עכנאי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: why is this oven named after a snake? It is setting up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on anything. It is a request to explain a strange name.

keyTerms.meaning: What? (a question word asking for an explanation)

phrases.english: What is akhnai?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the name given in step 1.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the name עכנאי.

steps.title: Surrounded with arguments like a coiled snake
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of שמואל explains that the חכמים surrounded the oven with arguments the way a snake coils, and ruled it טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: because they surrounded it with arguments like this snake, and declared it impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the oven is called 'snake' because the חכמים wrapped it in arguments the way a snake coils around itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The picture is a snake curled up in a circle. The חכמים surrounded the issue from every side with their reasoning, and in the end they ruled the oven טמא.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
That they surrounded it with words like this snake,
phrases.notes: The letters in square brackets are added in the corrected wording, making it 'surrounded it'.

phrases.english: and declared it impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים surrounded the oven with arguments like a coiled snake and ruled it טמא.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר brings every argument, but no one accepts
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that on that day רבי אליעזר gave every possible answer, and the חכמים did not accept any of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: on that day רבי אליעזר gave every answer in the world, but they did not accept them from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that begins the story of the debate. Logical arguments have failed, and this sets up the miracles that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that רבי אליעזר did not lose for lack of arguments. He used every argument there is, and the חכמים still did not agree. That is why he moves on to a new kind of proof.

phrases.english: It was taught: On that day

phrases.aramaic: הֵשִׁיב רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר כׇּל תְּשׁוּבוֹת שֶׁבָּעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer answered all the answers in the world,
but they did not accept from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the story of the debate behind the name.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's logical arguments were all rejected by the חכמים.

steps.title: First miracle: the carob tree moves
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says a carob tree will prove him right, and the tree uproots itself and moves 100 (or 400) אמות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: if the הלכה follows me, this carob tree will prove it. The carob tree was uprooted from its place 100 אמות, and some say 400 אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר stops arguing and asks for a miracle as proof. The carob tree jumps out of the ground and moves far away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new kind of proof: a sign from nature instead of reasoning. The question now is whether a miracle can decide הלכה.

phrases.english: He said to them: If the halakha is like me –
this carob tree will prove it.
The carob tree was uprooted from its place a hundred cubits,
and some say: four hundred cubits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After arguments fail, רבי אליעזר turns to a miracle.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The carob tree miraculously uprooting itself.

steps.title: A tree is no proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that one cannot bring a proof from a carob tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: one does not bring proof from a carob tree.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject the miracle. A tree moving does not decide הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not deny that the miracle happened. They deny that it counts as proof in a halachic debate.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מִן הֶחָרוּב.
phrases.english: They said to him: One does not bring proof from the carob tree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The carob tree miracle as evidence.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A miracle in nature is not a valid source of proof for הלכה.

steps.title: Second miracle: the stream flows backward
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר calls on the stream to prove him right, and the water flows backward.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said to them: if the הלכה follows me, the stream will prove it. The water of the stream turned backward.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר tries a second miracle. The stream reverses its direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The miracle is even more unnatural this time, since water flowing uphill goes against nature. רבי אליעזר is still trying to show that Heaven backs him.

phrases.english: He then said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתִי – אַמַּת הַמַּיִם יוֹכִיחוּ.
phrases.english: If the halakha is like me – the stream will prove it.
The stream's waters turned backward.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְאָמַר לָהֶם: אִם הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new miracle after the first was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: A stream is no proof
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that one cannot bring proof from a stream.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: one does not bring proof from a stream.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject the second miracle using the same reasoning as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern repeats. No matter how impressive the miracle is, it is not accepted as halachic evidence.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מֵאַמַּת הַמַּיִם.
phrases.english: They said to him: One does not bring proof from a stream.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אֵין מְבִיאִין רְאָיָה מֵאַמַּת הַמַּיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 7.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Natural wonders do not decide הלכה.

steps.title: Third miracle: the walls of the בית המדרש lean
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר calls on the walls of the בית המדרש, and they start leaning, about to fall.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said to them: if the הלכה follows me, the walls of the בית המדרש will prove it. The walls of the בית המדרש leaned, about to fall.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר asks the walls of the study hall itself to prove him right, and they begin to collapse inward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This time the miracle happens inside the place of Torah learning, which makes it more serious. It also threatens the people sitting there.

keyTerms.meaning: The walls of the study hall

phrases.english: He then said to them:
If the halakha is like me –
the walls of the study hall will prove it.
The walls of the study hall leaned to fall.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְאָמַר לָהֶם: אִם הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third miracle after the second was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The walls of the בית המדרש leaning.

steps.title: רבי יהושע scolds the walls
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rebukes the walls for getting involved in a debate between scholars. The walls neither fall nor straighten, and stay leaning.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע scolded them and said: if Torah scholars are debating each other in הלכה, what business is it of yours? They did not fall, out of respect for רבי יהושע, and did not straighten, out of respect for רבי אליעזר, and they still stand leaning.
steps.whatsHappening: Instead of answering רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע speaks to the walls directly and tells them to stay out of the debate. The walls end up stuck in between.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע's point is that deciding הלכה belongs to the scholars, not to walls or miracles. The walls stay half-leaning to honor both רבי יהושע and רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: Debating to win against each other

phrases.aramaic: גָּעַר בָּהֶם רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, אָמַר לָהֶם:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua scolded them, saying to them:
phrases.notes: 'Them' here means the walls, not the people.

phrases.english: If Torah scholars
are contending with each other in halakha,
what is your nature (to get involved)?

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נָפְלוּ מִפְּנֵי כְבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ,
phrases.english: They did not fall, because of the honor of Rabbi Yehoshua,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא זָקְפוּ מִפְּנֵי כְבוֹדוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר,
phrases.english: and they did not straighten, because of the honor of Rabbi Eliezer,
and they still remain leaning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the wall miracle, this time by speaking to the walls themselves.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Walls have no place in a halachic debate between scholars.

steps.title: Final proof: a בת קול from Heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר calls on Heaven, and a בת קול announces that the הלכה follows him everywhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said to them: if the הלכה follows me, Heaven will prove it. A בת קול came out and said: why are you arguing with רבי אליעזר, when the הלכה follows him in every place?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר brings his strongest proof: a voice from Heaven itself. The voice says he is right, and right everywhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This goes beyond nature. It is a direct statement from Heaven about the הלכה. The tension is now as high as it can get: will the חכמים reject even this?
steps.confusionAlert: The story does not end with the בת קול. In the next step, רבי יהושע answers even this voice, so don't conclude that רבי אליעזר's view became the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up one of the most famous principles in the גמרא: how human scholars decide הלכה even against a Heavenly voice.

phrases.english: He then said to them:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתִי – מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם יוֹכִיחוּ.
phrases.english: If the halakha is like me – Heaven will prove it.
A Divine Voice went out and said:
Why are you (disagreeing) with Rabbi Eliezer,
since the halakha is like him in every place.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר וְאָמַר לָהֶם: אִם הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתִי – מִן הַשָּׁמַיִם יוֹכִיחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The fourth and strongest proof, after the wall miracle was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That the הלכה follows רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבי יהושע declares: It is not in heaven
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע rejects the בת קול's proof with the פסוק 'לא בשמים היא'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stood up on his feet and said: 'It is not in heaven!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע stands up and rejects even the heavenly voice as a proof for רבי אליעזר. He quotes a פסוק from the תורה to do it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the strongest proof yet, a voice from Heaven itself, and it is still rejected. רבי יהושע uses the תורה's own words to say that heavenly signs do not decide הלכה. The גמרא will explain exactly what he meant in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: stood up on his feet, a sign of a serious, formal statement

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע is not doubting that the voice really came from Heaven. He is saying that even a real heavenly voice cannot decide a הלכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stood up on his feet
and said: "It is not in heaven!"

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the בת קול proof brought in step 11
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the whole idea that a heavenly voice can decide הלכה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The תורה is no longer in heaven, so heavenly signs carry no legal weight

steps.title: What does 'It is not in heaven' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this פסוק answers the בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'It is not in heaven' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story to ask what רבי יהושע meant by quoting this פסוק. This sets up רבי ירמיה's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to talk about the תורה being close to us, not about voices from Heaven. So the גמרא wants to know how it answers the בת קול.

phrases.english: What does "It is not in heaven" mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 12
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the פסוק 'לא בשמים היא' rules out the בת קול

steps.title: רבי ירמיה explains: the תורה follows the majority
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה explains that once the תורה was given at סיני, we decide by majority and ignore a בת קול.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: Since the תורה was already given at Mount סיני, we do not pay attention to a בת קול. You already wrote in the תורה at סיני: 'Follow the majority.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה explains רבי יהושע's words. Since the תורה was given at סיני, it now belongs to us. The תורה itself says to follow the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof against the בת קול comes from Heaven's own תורה. The תורה said 'אחרי רבים להטות,' so the majority of חכמים decides. Most חכמים disagreed with רבי אליעזר, so the הלכה does not follow him, even with a בת קול.

keyTerms.meaning: we do not pay attention to

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a basic rule of how הלכה works. Rulings are made by the חכמים using the תורה's rules, like following the majority, and not by miracles or heavenly voices.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
Since the Torah was already given from Mount Sinai,
we do not pay attention to a heavenly voice,
for You already wrote at Mount Sinai, in the Torah:
phrases.notes: "You" means הקדוש ברוך הוא. He is speaking straight to Heaven.

phrases.english: "Follow the majority to decide."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה: שֶׁכְּבָר נִתְּנָה תּוֹרָה מֵהַר סִינַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה, already given at סיני, commands following the majority, so a בת קול cannot override the majority of חכמים

steps.title: רבי נתן asks אליהו how Heaven reacted
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן meets אליהו and asks what הקדוש ברוך הוא did at that moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן met אליהו and asked him: What did הקדוש ברוך הוא do at that moment?
steps.whatsHappening: The story jumps forward to a later meeting between רבי נתן and אליהו הנביא. רבי נתן wants to know how Heaven reacted when רבי יהושע said 'לא בשמים היא.' This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the חכמים refused the בת קול, a reader might wonder whether Heaven was upset. רבי נתן asks exactly that question.

keyTerms.meaning: he met him, he found him
אליהו הנביא, who meets חכמים in many stories in the גמרא
The Holy One, Blessed be He

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan met Eliyahu
and said to him:
What did the Holy One, Blessed be He, do
at that moment?
phrases.notes: He means the moment רבי יהושע said "It is not in heaven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how Heaven responded to the rejection in steps 12-14
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Heaven's reaction to the חכמים overruling the בת קול

steps.title: God smiled: My children have defeated Me
steps.stepSummary: אליהו answers that הקדוש ברוך הוא smiled and said, 'My children have defeated Me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: He was smiling and saying, 'My children have defeated Me! My children have defeated Me!'
steps.whatsHappening: אליהו says that הקדוש ברוך הוא was not angry. He smiled and was pleased that His children had won the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the חכמים were right to follow the majority and not the בת קול. Heaven itself approves of the system it gave in the תורה. The smile shows joy, like a parent whose child beats him in a debate.
steps.whatToRemember: The halachic part of the story ends here. The majority of חכמים decides הלכה, even against a בת קול, and Heaven approves.

phrases.english: He said to him: He was smiling and saying,
"My children have defeated Me! My children have defeated Me!"

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי נתן's question from step 15
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Heaven was pleased and accepted that the חכמים had won

steps.title: The pure items are burned and רבי אליעזר is placed in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: On that day the חכמים burned everything רבי אליעזר had ruled pure and voted to place him in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: On that day they brought all the טהרות that רבי אליעזר had ruled pure and burned them in fire. They voted about him and 'blessed' him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes back to that day. The חכמים put their ruling into practice by burning the items. They also placed רבי אליעזר in נידוי for refusing to accept the majority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everything prepared in the oven that רבי אליעזר called pure is treated as טמא, since the majority ruled against him. Placing him in נידוי shows how seriously they took his refusal to accept the majority ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: items handled in purity, here food made with the oven
literally 'they blessed him,' a polite way of saying they placed him in נידוי

steps.confusionAlert: 'ברכוהו' does not mean they blessed him. It is a polite way of saying they placed him in נידוי.

phrases.english: They said: On that day
they brought all the pure items
that Rabbi Eliezer had declared pure
and burned them in fire.
And they voted about him and "blessed" him.
phrases.notes: "Blessed" is a gentle way of saying they put him in נידוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ: אוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם הֵבִיאוּ כׇּל טְהָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the practical results of the majority ruling
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The items רבי אליעזר ruled pure were burned as טמא, and he was placed in נידוי

steps.title: Who will tell him?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask who will go and tell רבי אליעזר that he is in נידוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And they said: Who will go and tell him?
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים face a hard job: someone has to give רבי אליעזר this painful news. This question sets up רבי עקיבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question shows that how the news is given matters a lot. Telling a great חכם he is in נידוי needs great care.

keyTerms.meaning: will tell him, will inform him

phrases.english: And they said: Who will go and tell him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the נידוי in step 17
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who should deliver the news of the נידוי

steps.title: רבי עקיבא volunteers
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא volunteers so that an unsuitable person will not deliver the news badly and destroy the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to them: I will go. Otherwise someone unsuitable may go and tell him, and he would end up destroying the whole world.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא, רבי אליעזר's student, offers to go himself. He is afraid that someone else might tell him harshly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא understands that a hurt from such a great צדיק could bring disaster on the world. So the message must come from someone who loves him and will speak gently.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲנִי אֵלֵךְ
phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to them: I will go,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא יֵלֵךְ אָדָם שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן וְיוֹדִיעוֹ
phrases.english: in case an unsuitable person goes and tells him,

phrases.aramaic: וְנִמְצָא מַחְרִיב אֶת כָּל הָעוֹלָם כּוּלּוֹ.
phrases.english: and it would turn out that he destroys the entire world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לָהֶם רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא: אֲנִי אֵלֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי עקיבא will go, to make sure the news is given with care

steps.title: רבי עקיבא comes dressed in black
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא dresses in black and sits four אמות away from רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did רבי עקיבא do? He dressed in black, wrapped himself in black, and sat in front of him at a distance of four אמות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא does not say the news out loud. He shows it through his black clothes and by sitting four אמות away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Black clothes show mourning and pain. Four אמות is the distance people keep from someone in נידוי, so his seat itself hints at the news.

keyTerms.meaning: black clothes, a sign of mourning
four cubits, the distance kept from a person in נידוי

phrases.english: What did Rabbi Akiva do?
He dressed in black and wrapped himself in black,
and sat before him at a distance of four amos.
phrases.notes: That is the distance people keep from someone in נידוי, so the seat itself sends the message.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes how רבי עקיבא carried out his offer from step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי עקיבא hints at the נידוי through mourning clothes and distance

steps.title: רבי אליעזר asks what is different today
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks רבי עקיבא why today is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said to him: עקיבא, what is today compared to other days?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר notices the strange behavior and asks what happened. This sets up רבי עקיבא's gentle answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא's signs worked: רבי אליעזר sees that something is wrong and asks. Now the news can come out softly, as an answer to his question.

keyTerms.meaning: what makes today different from other days?

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer said to him: Akiva,
what is different about today from other days?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר: עֲקִיבָא, מָה יוֹם מִיָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי עקיבא's behavior in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי עקיבא is acting like a mourner

steps.title: רבי עקיבא gently gives the news
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers politely that the חבירים seem to be keeping away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: My teacher, it seems to me that your colleagues are keeping away from you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא tells him the news in the softest possible way. He does not say 'you are in נידוי'; he says the others seem to be keeping their distance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The truth is that the חכמים separated רבי אליעזר from themselves. רבי עקיבא turns it around, saying they are separating from him, and adds 'it seems to me,' to soften the blow.

phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher,
it seems to me that your colleagues are keeping away from you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אליעזר's question from step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is in נידוי, said in gentle words

steps.title: רבי אליעזר accepts the נידוי
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר tears his clothes, takes off his shoes, and sits on the ground.
steps.simpleTranslation: He too tore his clothes, took off his shoes, slipped down, and sat on the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר understands the news and acts like a person in נידוי or mourning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tearing clothes, removing shoes, and sitting on the ground are signs of mourning that a person in נידוי keeps. רבי אליעזר accepts the נידוי, but he is in deep pain.

phrases.english: He too tore his clothes
and took off his shoes,
and slipped down and sat on the ground.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַף הוּא קָרַע בְּגָדָיו וְחָלַץ מִנְעָלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי אליעזר's reaction to the news in step 22
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר takes on the practices of a person in נידוי

steps.title: His tears damage the world's crops
steps.stepSummary: When רבי אליעזר cried, a third of the olives, wheat, and barley were struck. Some say even dough spoiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: His eyes streamed with tears, and the world was struck: a third of the olives, a third of the wheat, and a third of the barley. Some say even dough in a woman's hands spoiled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא describes what happened when רבי אליעזר cried. His pain brought damage to the food of the whole world.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is exactly what רבי עקיבא feared in step 19. Even with his gentle approach, the hurt of such a great צדיק damaged the world. The 'some say' opinion adds that even dough already being kneaded was ruined.

phrases.english: His eyes streamed with tears,
and the world was struck:
a third of the olives,
a third of the wheat, and a third of the barley.

phrases.aramaic: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף בָּצֵק שֶׁבִּידֵי אִשָּׁה טָפַח.
phrases.english: And some say: even dough in a woman's hands spoiled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the results of רבי אליעזר's pain from step 23
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's tears brought damage to the world's crops

steps.title: Wherever רבי אליעזר looked, things burned
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that there was great anger that day, and every place רבי אליעזר looked at burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: There was great anger on that day, for every place that רבי אליעזר set his eyes on was burned.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds one more detail about that day: there was great anger, and anything רבי אליעזר looked at burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds to the damage in the last step. It is not only crops that suffered: there was anger in the world that day, and his look alone set things on fire.
steps.whatToRemember: The majority ruled against רבי אליעזר, and Heaven agreed. Even so, hurting a great חכם brought terrible results, which is why רבי עקיבא took such care.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אַף גָּדוֹל הָיָה בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
phrases.english: It was taught: There was great anger on that day,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁבְּכָל מָקוֹם שֶׁנָּתַן בּוֹ עֵינָיו רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר – נִשְׂרַף.
phrases.english: for every place that Rabbi Eliezer set his eyes on was burned.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אַף גָּדוֹל הָיָה בְּאוֹתוֹ הַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ברייתא describing more damage from that day
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There was great anger that day, and whatever רבי אליעזר looked at burned

steps.title: A huge wave threatens רבן גמליאל at sea
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל is on a boat when a giant wave threatens to drown him, and he senses it is because of רבי אליעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל was also traveling on a boat, and a huge wave rose up to drown him. He said: I think this is only because of רבי אליעזר בן הורקנוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues from the anger of that day. Now the punishment reaches רבן גמליאל, the leader who was behind the excommunication.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' (וְאַף) links this to the damage described in the steps before it. רבן גמליאל himself understands that the wave is a heavenly response to the pain caused to רבי אליעזר.

phrases.english: And even Rabban Gamliel
was traveling on a boat.
A huge wave rose over him to drown him.
He said: It seems to me
that this is only
because of Rabbi Eliezer ben Hyrcanus.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל הָיָה בָּא בִּסְפִינָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of results of רבי אליעזר's pain, now reaching רבן גמליאל himself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A wave threatened to drown רבן גמליאל, and he understood it was because of the pain caused to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל's prayer calms the sea
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells ה׳ he acted only for Heaven's honor, to prevent disputes in Israel, and the sea calms down.
steps.simpleTranslation: He stood up and said: Master of the World, You know that I did not do this for my own honor or for my family's honor. I did it for Your honor, so that arguments would not multiply in Israel. The sea calmed down.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל explains to ה׳ why he excommunicated רבי אליעזר, and ה׳ accepts his reason for now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He argues that his motive was pure: keeping the authority of the majority so that Torah would not split into many disputes. The sea calming shows that his intentions were accepted, but as the next steps show, this does not fully end the danger.

keyTerms.meaning: Master of the World, a way of addressing ה׳
It is revealed and known before You

phrases.english: He stood on his feet and said:
Master of the World,
it is revealed and known before You
that I did not act for my own honor,
nor did I act for the honor of my father's house,
but rather for Your honor,
so that arguments would not multiply in Israel.
The sea calmed from its raging.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָמַד עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל responds to the danger described in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Acting purely for Heaven's honor, to prevent disputes, saved רבן גמליאל from drowning.

steps.title: אימא שלום guards her husband's prayers
steps.stepSummary: אימא שלום, wife of רבי אליעזר and sister of רבן גמליאל, stops her husband from saying נפילת אפים.
steps.simpleTranslation: אימא שלום, the wife of רבי אליעזר, was the sister of רבן גמליאל. From that incident onward, she would not let רבי אליעזר fall on his face in prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא introduces a new character who is caught between the two sides. This step sets up the rest of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because she is married to one side and is the sister of the other, she understood that her husband's prayer of pain could harm her brother. So she made sure he never said the personal prayer of נפילת אפים.

keyTerms.meaning: Wife of רבי אליעזר and sister of רבן גמליאל
To fall on his face, meaning to say תחנון

phrases.english: Imma Shalom,
the wife of Rabbi Eliezer,
was the sister of Rabban Gamliel.
From that incident onward,

phrases.aramaic: לָא הֲוָה שָׁבְקָה לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
phrases.english: she would not let Rabbi Eliezer
fall on his face.
phrases.notes: This is the prayer of תחנון, where a person bows his head and pours out his heart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story forward and explains how רבן גמליאל was protected afterward.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אימא שלום prevented her husband's pained prayers in order to protect her brother.

steps.title: A mix-up about ראש חודש
steps.stepSummary: One day she got confused about whether it was ראש חודש, so she did not stop him.
steps.simpleTranslation: One day was around ראש חודש, and she mixed up whether the month was full or short.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how she slipped up once. She thought it was ראש חודש, when no one falls on his face, so she didn't watch him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A month can have 30 days (full) or 29 days (short). She counted wrong, thought it was ראש חודש, and assumed he would not say תחנון anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: ראש חודש, the start of the month

phrases.english: One day was around Rosh Chodesh,
and she mixed up a full month with a short month.
phrases.notes: She thought it was ראש חודש, when תחנון isn't said, but it really wasn't.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how her careful guarding failed one time.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A calendar mistake left רבי אליעזר unwatched.

steps.title: Another version: a poor man at the door
steps.stepSummary: Others say a poor man came to the door, and she went out to give him bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say a poor man came and stood at the door, and she brought bread out to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of why she wasn't watching her husband at that moment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions end the same way: for a short time she wasn't watching him. Here the reason is a מצוה, giving bread to a poor man, rather than a calendar mistake.

phrases.english: Some say:
a poor man came and stood at the door,
and she brought bread out to him.

steps.alternativePossibleLabel: Alternative version of the previous step (מימרא)
steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי אֲתָא עַנְיָא וְקָאֵי אַבָּבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different explanation for the same moment described in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Another version: she stepped away to feed a poor man.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל dies
steps.stepSummary: She finds him praying on his face and tells him he has killed her brother, and just then the שופר announces רבן גמליאל's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: She found him fallen on his face. She said to him: Get up, you have killed my brother. Meanwhile a שופר blast came from רבן גמליאל's house announcing that he had died.
steps.whatsHappening: The moment she feared happens: רבי אליעזר prays in pain, and her brother dies right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her words come before the news arrives, so she already knew what his prayer would cause. The שופר was blown to announce the death of the נשיא.

keyTerms.meaning: Meanwhile, in the middle of this

phrases.english: She found him fallen on his face.
She said to him: Get up,
you have killed my brother.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Meanwhile a shofar blast went out
from the house of Rabban Gamliel, announcing that he had died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows what happened because she stepped away.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר's pained prayer caused רבן גמליאל's death.

steps.title: How did you know?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר asks his wife how she knew his prayer would kill her brother.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: How did you know?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר is surprised that she said it before the news came, so he asks for her source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question asking for information, not a challenge. It sets up her answer, which explains the lesson of the whole story.

keyTerms.meaning: How did you know? (spoken to a woman)

phrases.english: He said to her: How did you know?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how she could have predicted the event in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How אימא שלום knew that her husband's prayer would bring about her brother's death.

steps.title: The gates of hurt feelings are never locked
steps.stepSummary: She answers with a family tradition: all heavenly gates may close except the gates for prayers of people hurt by words.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said to him: This is what I received from my grandfather's house: All the gates are locked, except for the gates of hurtful words.
steps.whatsHappening: אימא שלום gives the rule behind the whole story. The prayer of a person who was hurt by words always gets through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This connects the story back to the topic of the סוגיא, אונאת דברים. רבי אליעזר had been deeply hurt, so his prayer went straight up, even against a great and well-meaning leader.

keyTerms.meaning: I received this as a tradition
Gates, here meaning the gates of Heaven for prayer

steps.whatToRemember: The story of רבי אליעזר ends with its main lesson: the cry of someone hurt by words is always heard. Even רבן גמליאל, who acted for Heaven's sake, was punished.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why the גמרא tells the whole story here. It shows how serious אונאת דברים is, which is the subject the סוגיא returns to right after this.

phrases.english: She said to him:
This is what I received from the house of my father's father:
All the gates are locked
except for the gates of hurtful words.
phrases.notes: She means the gates that let in the prayers of someone who was hurt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of how she knew.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A family tradition that the prayer of someone hurt by words is never blocked.

steps.title: Hurting or oppressing a גר
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that hurting a גר with words breaks three לאוין, and oppressing him breaks two.
steps.simpleTranslation: תנו רבנן: Someone who hurts a גר with words violates three לאוין. Someone who oppresses him violates two.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא leaves the story and goes back to הלכה with a new ברייתא about the גר. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will look for the sources of these numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two cases: אונאה, meaning hurtful words, and לחיצה, meaning oppressing him in other ways. It gives a count of prohibitions for each, but it does not yet say where these prohibitions come from.

keyTerms.meaning: One who hurts someone, here with words

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who hurts a convert with words
violates three prohibitions.
And one who oppresses him violates two.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the story ends with a lesson about hurtful words, the גמרא returns to halacha with a ruling about hurting a גר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hurting a גר with words breaks three לאוין, and oppressing him breaks two.

steps.title: Oppressing a גר also has three לאוין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: oppressing a גר is also written in three לאוין, just like hurting him with words.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is hurting with words different, that it has three prohibitions ('Do not mistreat a convert,' 'When a convert lives with you, do not mistreat him,' 'Do not mistreat your fellow,' and a convert is included in 'fellow')? Oppressing him also has three ('Do not oppress him,' 'Do not oppress a convert,' 'Do not be to him like a creditor,' and a convert is included in that)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא from step 34. That ברייתא said hurting a גר with words breaks three לאוין, but oppressing him breaks only two. The גמרא shows that oppressing him also has three פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא itself gives no sources. The גמרא supplies them for hurtful words: two פסוקים speak about the גר, and a third general פסוק ('his fellow') includes him. The same method works for oppressing: two פסוקים about the גר plus the general 'do not be like a creditor', which also includes him. So the ברייתא's count of two for oppressing seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why should this case be treated differently?
One who hurts someone with words
One who oppresses him (pressures him, often with money matters)
Like a creditor, someone pushing hard to collect a loan

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying that hurting a גר with words is less serious. It is only fixing the count for oppressing, which turns out to be three too.

phrases.english: What is different about one who mistreats with words
that three prohibitions are written about it:
"And you shall not mistreat a convert",
"And when a convert lives with you in your land
you shall not mistreat him",
"And you shall not mistreat, each man his fellow",
and a convert is included in "his fellow."
For one who oppresses him, three are also written:
"Nor shall you oppress him",
"And you shall not oppress a convert",
"And you shall not be to him like a creditor",
and a convert is included in that!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא מְאַנֶּה, דִּכְתִיבִי שְׁלֹשָׁה לָאוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the count of לאוין in the ברייתא of step 34
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that oppressing a גר breaks only two לאוין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same counting method that gives three for words (two specific פסוקים plus a general one) also gives three for oppressing.

steps.title: Both kinds of hurting a גר break three לאוין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that both hurting a גר with words and oppressing him break three לאוין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, both this one and that one break three prohibitions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts its own challenge and fixes the count. Hurting a גר with words and oppressing him each break three לאוין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's split of three versus two is dropped. Since each one has two פסוקים about the גר plus one general פסוק, both are counted as three.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, it must be (correcting what was said before)
Both this one and that one

steps.whatToRemember: Hurting a גר with words and oppressing him each break three לאוין.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה.
phrases.english: Rather, both this one and that one are with three.
phrases.notes: He means both the one who hurts with words and the one who oppresses break three prohibitions.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 35 and corrects the count
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both hurting a גר with words and oppressing him break three לאוין.

steps.title: Why the תורה warns so many times about the גר
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר הגדול teaches that the Torah warns about the גר in 36 (or 46) places, because his inclination is bad.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: רבי אליעזר הגדול says: Why did the Torah warn about a convert in thirty-six places, and some say in forty-six places? Because his inclination is bad.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא adds a bigger idea: the Torah warns about the גר many, many times. רבי אליעזר הגדול explains why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that a גר may easily slip back to his old ways. If he is hurt, he might leave, so the Torah adds extra warnings to protect him. This fits with the many לאוין just counted.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
His inclination is bad; he may easily go back to his old ways

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi Eliezer the Great says:
For what reason did the Torah warn
in thirty-six places,
and some say: in forty-six places,
about a convert?
Because his inclination is bad.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands from counting לאוין about the גר to the reason the Torah warns about him so often
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The Torah warns about the גר in 36 or 46 places because he may easily return to his old ways.

steps.title: What does 'you were strangers in Egypt' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the reason in the פסוק, 'for you were strangers in the land of מצרים', is teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the meaning of the פסוק: "And you shall not mistreat a convert nor oppress him, for you were strangers in the land of Egypt"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks about the end of the פסוק. Why does the Torah add 'for you were strangers in מצרים'? This sets up רבי נתן's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is about the logic of the reason the Torah gives. What does our past in מצרים have to do with how we speak to a גר?

keyTerms.meaning: What is the meaning of what is written?

phrases.english: What is that which is written:
"And you shall not mistreat a convert nor oppress him,
for you were strangers in the land of Egypt"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וְגֵר לֹא תוֹנֶה וְלֹא תִלְחָצֶנּוּ כִּי גֵרִים הֱיִיתֶם בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרָיִם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to explaining the reason the Torah itself gives for the warning
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the reason 'for you were strangers in מצרים' teaches about how to treat a גר

steps.title: Do not point out your own flaw in someone else
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן explains: do not mention to your friend a flaw that you have yourself.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: רבי נתן says: A flaw that is in you, do not say to your friend.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא from רבי נתן. Since we were once strangers too, we should not insult a גר for being a stranger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah's reason is not only 'remember how it felt.' It is also: you have the same 'flaw', so you have no right to point it out in him. Mocking a גר for being an outsider is mocking something that is true of yourself.

phrases.english: We learned: Rabbi Natan says:
A flaw that is in you, do not say to your friend.

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנֵינָא, רַבִּי נָתָן אוֹמֵר: מוּם שֶׁבְּךָ אַל תֹּאמַר לַחֲבֵרֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 38
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the Jewish people were strangers themselves, they must not point out the 'stranger' flaw in a גר.

steps.title: A popular saying: don't mention hanging in a family with a hanging
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up רבי נתן with a saying: in a family where someone was hanged, don't even say 'hang up a fish.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what people say: One who had someone hanged in his family should not say to his fellow, "Hang up a fish."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רבי נתן's idea with a well-known saying. If your family has a painful 'flaw', you should not even use words that remind people of it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The saying makes the lesson sharper: avoid not only open insults but even innocent words that touch a sore spot. In the same way, we must be very careful in how we speak to a גר.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what people say (a common saying)
A hanging, someone who was hanged

phrases.english: And this is what people say:
One who had someone hanged in his family,
should not say to his fellow:
"Hang up a fish."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי נתן's teaching with a popular saying
steps.raayaObject: רבי נתן's rule: do not point out in someone else a flaw you have yourself
steps.raayaSupportSource: A common saying about a family with a hanging not mentioning hanging
steps.whatToRemember: We were strangers in מצרים, so we must never put down a גר for being a stranger. Do not point out in others a flaw you share.

steps.title: New משנה: a seller may not mix batches of produce
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that one may not mix produce with other produce, even new with new.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: One may not mix produce with produce, even new produce with new produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא's discussion of hurting a גר ends, and a new משנה begins. It is about selling honestly: a seller may not mix one batch of produce into another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'even' shows how strict the rule is. Even when both batches are new, and it looks like the buyer loses nothing, the seller still may not mix them.

keyTerms.meaning: משנה; a new משנה is starting

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One may not mix produce with produce,
phrases.notes: This means produce from one supplier mixed with produce from another, when selling.

phrases.english: even new with new.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of hurting a גר ends
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller may not mix one batch of produce with another, even new produce with new produce.
